Step 9 complete. Report at `research/frontier-13-alpha-a-step9.md`.

## What the sweep found

**136 declines re-tested**, not the ~90 the brief estimated. **Seven reasons were false or misattributed.** Two were decisive, and both results are now built and judged:

- **Batch 6's floor/ceiling decline** claimed "the required real floor definition is absent on disk." `lem-integer-part` is published on `limits-of-real-functions`, which *is* in the adjunctions closure, and states exactly the floor. Built `ex-ceiling-and-floor-are-adjoint-to-the-inclusion-of-the-integers` — the full adjoint triple ⌈−⌉ ⊣ J ⊣ ⌊−⌋.
- **Batch 2's Q₈ decline** rested on "Q₈ would first have to be constructed" — the disposition the 2026-08-11 rule retired — and named no destination page. Built three items; the counterexample refutes a strictly narrower statement than the existing C_{p²} witness (nonabelian middle group).

Batch 5's quaternion row asserted "no quaternion-algebra dependency exists in the library spine" — false on the same evidence, though the decline survives on different, now-recorded ground. Two "squaring the circle" rows deferred to a transcendence page that exists nowhere in the plan.

**Every deferral now names a licensing page id.** Before this sweep, 52 of 68 named only prose ("the later monoidal track"), which is indistinguishable from a drop.

**The Chernikov/Zhao section titles were already fixed** — I verified all three against the source PDFs with `pypdf` rather than trusting the prior report. Nothing to route.

**Zero `proved_here: false` items** across all 467 — the external fallback was never used.

## One thing I have to flag about my own work

The four new items took seven judge findings to clear, **all of them mine**, and five were inflated or unlicensed citations — the run's dominant defect class, committed by the Alpha whose step-6b charge was that class. Round 1 attributed "every group of prime order is cyclic" to a theorem that says nothing of the kind. The mathematics was correct throughout; no finding touched an argument.

The counterexample went five repair rounds, well past the twice-touched threshold. Rounds 4 and 5 sat at the 30-second boundary and I could have adjudicated them nonfatal; I repaired instead because at step 9 repair is free.

**Lane asymmetry worth carrying into step 10:** Terra produced 6 of 7 findings; DeepSeek passed 5 of the 6 rounds Terra rejected. The cross-family screen was the weaker reader here — the opposite of the lineup's rationale.

All gates green after the repairs, including `proof-contract --strict --require-reviewed` (393/393), both judge lanes passing all four new items, and the standing closure check over 467 items / 1572 dependency edges with 0 out-of-closure, 0 cross-pair, 0 B-leaf.

Also worth knowing: `research/frontier-13-RESUME.md` still reads "Step 3 Alpha scaffold review in flight." A session recovering from it would replay step 3.
